system.summary: Words erased from a clear letter and replaced by printer's reference marks (*, §, §§, †); the same mark stands for unrelated fillers, so the marks carry no values.

prior_solution.where: Washington Papers editors: no key identified; nothing else found.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the unsolved catalogue (item 486) with the project's standard contributor brief; nothing else.

solution.what: Read the letter and the editors' source note on Founders Online 03-11-02-0272.
Copied the letter with its five marks (* § §§ † §) and the slot each fills to transcription.txt.
Tested whether the marks are a substitution or code: § stands for a number (united force) and for a route or carrier (baggage sent by §), so one sign has two unrelated fillers.

Read Washington to Smallwood 17 Sept 1777 (junction with the main army, the likely sense of §§) and Smallwood to Washington 15 Sept 1777 (fear of an intercepted express); one web search for other printings or the Rubinfine catalogue.
Tried the LoC George Washington Papers search for the Sprague transcript image; blocked by a bot check, not bypassed.

outcome.method_basis: The letter is clear English with five words erased and replaced by printer's reference marks; § fills both a number and a route, so the marks are blanks, not cipher values.
outcome.notes: The erased words are lost; context from Washington's 17 Sept letter suggests §§ hid the junction with the main army, but nothing is filled in.
